components.description: Flagged APOD frame with perforated edges and orange tape.
components.css: .ds-film-window { position: relative; background: #ffffff; color: #000000; } .ds-film-window::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #000000; pointer-events: none; z-index: 2; } .ds-tape-flag { position: absolute; top: -1px; left: 24px; width: 48px; height: 18px; background: #e85d04; transform: rotate(-2deg); z-index: 10; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-tape-flag::after { content: ''; position: absolute; right: -6px; top: 0; width: 12px; height: 100%; background: #e85d04; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 50%, 0 100%); } .ds-perf-edge { height: 8px; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, #000000 0, #000000 6px, transparent 6px, transparent 14px); background-size: 14px 8px; } .ds-perf-edge--bottom { transform: rotate(180deg); } .ds-film-aperture { aspect-ratio: 16/10; background: #000000; }

narrative.overview:
Stargaze is an analog editing bench for cosmic imagery — today's APOD is the frame flagged with orange tape on a perforated select rail; the archive is the strip you scrub frame by frame; headlines hang below like trims pinned to the bench. The atmosphere is brutally editorial: true black ground, flag orange ink, white type, and a persistent film-grain overlay. NASA photography breaks through the austerity; the UI frames it like physical film stock, not glass cards.

Every migrated route (home, gallery, gallery detail, news, about, sign-in, sign-up) shares one surface language. Section labels speak bench vocabulary — CAPTION WINDOW, RECENT SELECTS, HUNG TRIMS, ADJACENT FRAMES — and the shell wraps all pages in perforated film rails above the nav and above the footer.
keyCharacteristics: True black (#000000) canvas with fixed film-grain overlay at 12% opacity
Flag orange (#e85d04) as the sole chromatic accent — rails, tape flags, CTAs, active states, dates
Barlow Condensed throughout; uppercase labels with wide letter-spacing via .label-caps
Perforated film edges, flagged frames with orange tape, horizontal film-strip rails, hung-trim news cards
Sharp rectangular geometry — 2px white borders, zero border-radius on interactive surfaces
Shell: 56px nav with orange bottom rule, 52px footer, max-w-6xl content column
No icon library on migrated pages; meaning carried by type, borders, and bench metaphors

rules.name: The Flag Orange Rule
rules.body: #e85d04 is the only chromatic accent across migrated surfaces. Reserve it for selection, rails, tape, CTAs, and emphasis — roughly one-third of visible UI ink.

rules.name: The True Black Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds stay #000000. Depth comes from photography, grain, and borders — never gray page fills or glass translucency stacks.

rules.name: The Opacity Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Differentiate supporting copy with white opacity steps (/80, /60, /50, /40) — not text-gray-* utilities.

rules.name: The Barlow-Only Rule
rules.body: No secondary typeface. Weight, case, and tracking create hierarchy.

rules.name: The Bench Label Rule
rules.body: Section landmarks and navigation use .label-caps uppercase with wide tracking. Content titles within sections use bold uppercase at larger sizes without the label preset.

rules.name: The Flat Bench Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels are flat black with 2px borders. No drop shadows on migrated surfaces.

rules.name: The Grain Always Rule
rules.body: The film-grain overlay stays active on every page; it is ambient texture, not a hero-only effect.

dos: Do frame today's APOD in a film-window with perforated edges and an orange tape flag.
Do use flag orange for rails, section kickers, active frame states, and primary CTAs.
Do keep all migrated surfaces on true black with 2px white structural borders and square corners.
Do use .label-caps for navigation, section labels, dates, and form labels.
Do structure home as bench workflow: flagged select → caption window → strip → hung trims.
Do maintain the film-grain overlay and perforated shell rails on every page.
Do use max-w-prose on long explanatory copy for comfortable reading measure.
donts: Don't use border-radius, glass blur, or drop shadows on new migrated surfaces.
Don't introduce accent colors beyond flag orange (except photography itself).
Don't use icon libraries or glyph decorations on migrated pages — the bench metaphor carries wayfinding.
Don't use text-gray-* utilities — use white opacity steps.
Don't revert to the prior Orbitron/violet observatory glass system on migrated routes.
Don't stack deprioritized legacy sections (missions, timeline, community) on the home bench.
